qc.label_under_test: The 'as' (or the 'a' just after it) when me, us or you is labelled back: an earlier clause has me, us or you seeing, thinking of, regarding or treating someone else as something, and a following clause has that other person see, think of, regard or treat me, us or you 'as' something in return; the return can end in a noun or an adjective. Weak: the same return clause aimed at a third person (him, her, them, a brother), a one-way label of me, us or you with no earlier clause, me labelled first and then answering back, the bare form without 'as' (thinks me foolish, considers me a fool), and official appointments to a post.

neighbours.label: The 'as' (or the 'a' just after it) when me, us or you is labelled back: an earlier clause has me, us or you seeing, thinking of, regarding, treating, describing or hailing someone else as something, and a following clause has that other person or group see, think of, regard, treat, describe or hail me, us or you 'as' something in return; the return can end in a noun or an adjective. Weaker but can still fire: the same two-way mirror written entirely with third-person pronouns (he and her, they and him). Weak: mirrors between named people or noun phrases (the coach and the striker), a return clause aimed at a third person after an earlier clause about me, us or you, a one-way label of me, us or you with no earlier clause, me labelled first and then answering back, the bare form without 'as' even inside a mirror (thinks me a fool), a return framed as what someone should do, and official appointments to a post.
fire: I always saw her as a mentor, and she came to see me as a friend.
We treated the newcomers as family, and in time they treated us as family too.
You regard him as a rival, but he regards you as an ally.
I thought of the old fisherman as a hero, and he thought of me as a nuisance.
We described the villagers as generous hosts, and they described us as polite guests.
If you see them as enemies, they will see you as an enemy as well.
I hailed the captain as a genius, and he hailed me as a worthy successor.
We regarded our neighbours as eccentric, and they no doubt regarded us as boring.
quiet: I always saw her at the market, and she came to visit me on Sundays.
We treated the newcomers to dinner, and in time they treated us to lunch too.
You admire him a lot, but he barely notices you.
I thought about the old fisherman often, and he wrote to me every winter.
We praised the villagers for their kindness, and they thanked us for our help.
If you ignore them, they will ignore you as well.
I greeted the captain warmly, and he shook my hand firmly.
We liked our neighbours a great deal, and they liked us back.

predictions: Most fire items above 0.20 (the conditional 'if you see them as' item is the riskiest); near misses all below 0.30.
